title: SUDO: From Scientific Publications to Global Scholarly Discourse
abstract: arXiv:2610.33018v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Scholarly Knowledge Graphs (SKGs) support literature search, scientific discovery, and agent-assisted research. Yet, most approaches to SKG construction pre-specify the knowledge unit to be represented, typically named scholarly entities or contribution-level statements, and retain only the publication content expressible through that unit. This choice produces two dominant yet distinct paradigms: concept-centric SKGs that preserve entities and local relations, and statement-centric SKGs that capture high-level discourse in sentences. In both cases, the graph reflects a chosen extraction target rather than how a paper constructs and communicates knowledge. translated_title: SUDO：从科学出版物到全球学术话语
translated_abstract: 学术知识图谱支持文献检索、科学发现以及智能体辅助研究。然而，大多数构建学术知识图谱的方法都预先指定了要表示的知识单元，通常是命名的学术实体或贡献层面的语句，并且只保留能够通过该单元表达的出版物内容。这种选择产生了两种主流但截然不同的范式：以概念为中心的学术知识图谱，它保留实体和局部关系；以及以语句为中心的学术知识图谱，它以句子的形式捕捉高层话语。在这两种情况下，图谱所反映的都是选定的抽取目标，而非论文本身如何构建和传达知识。我们提出了SUDO，即学术上层话语本体，它定义了知识元素如何被组织和关联，从而形成论文的研究叙事，即其学术话语。利用能够跨领域和任务泛化的语言学原则，SUDO使每篇出版物……
tldr: 该论文提出SUDO（学术上层话语本体），通过定义知识元素的组织与关联方式来刻画论文的学术话语结构，突破了现有学术知识图谱构建中预指定抽取单元的局限。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces SUDO, a Scholarly Upper Discourse Ontology that defines how knowledge elements are organized and related to form a paper's scholarly discourse, overcoming the limitation of pre-specified extraction units in existing scholarly knowledge graph construction approaches.
